notes:
Summary: Orchid Harbor is a mid-to-large healthcare IT provider evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private deployment for clinical document ingestion, codification, and triage chatbots. Primary drivers: latency SLOs for clinician-facing chat (p95 < 200ms target), deterministic throughput for nightly batch embedding jobs, and strict residency/KMS/audit requirements.

SLA / Contract priorities observed: 
- Uptime target: they are pushing for 99.995% (approx ~26 minutes downtime/year). They view anything below 99.99% as unacceptable for production clinician workflows.
- Credit schedule: customer requested graduated credits tied to monthly uptime % (e.g., 99.995-100% = 0%, 99.99-99.995 = 10% credits, 99.9-99.99 = 30% credits, <99.9 = 50% credits); legal asked for examples of historical availability to support negotiation.
- Maintenance windows: MUST avoid clinical peak hours Mon-Fri 06:00-20:00 ET; willing to accept pre-scheduled maintenance 2x/year during weekend windows only. Emergency patching allowed but needs 72h post-incident RCA and provided fallbacks.
- Support response times: require P1 (service down) 30-minute response, P2 (severe degradation) 2-hour response, 24x7 escalation path to engineering for P1. Seeking optional premium SRE engagement.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial commit is 32 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs (estimate), with burst-to-shared capacity for seasonal spikes. They want predictable scaling cost model and an option to expand reserves at fixed uplift.
- Throughput guarantees: 24/7 baseline throughput commitment for embeddings pipeline: 200K tokens/min sustained; infra to be validated in a 2-week perf POC.
- Latency SLOs: clinician chat p95 <200ms (token generation + network), p99 <450ms; embeddings batch not latency-critical but throughput bound.
- Fallbacks & routing: require multi-zone routing and automatic fallback to smaller local model if Dedicated pool is degraded; also want explicit fallbacks documented in SLA annex.

Procurement negotiation notes / concessions under discussion: 
- Redwood proposed 99.99% baseline SLA for Dedicated with optional uplift to 99.995% at 18% price uplift. Customer asked for proof points of current tenants hitting 99.995% for 6+ months.
- Credit schedule in Redwood template is 10-20% for outages; customer pushing for steeper credits for high-severity incidents. Need legal trade-offs.
- Maintenance: Redwood prefers weekly 4-hour maintenance windows; Orchid Harbor insists on weekend-only scheduled maintenance for prod pools. Potential compromise: weekly windows only for non-prod, and quarterly weekend prod windows.
- Support: Redwood standard 24/7 support with business-hour hotline; customer requires guaranteed 30-min P1 response — pricing for prioritized SRE on-call discussed.

POC / Validation plan: 
- Week 0: Contract NDA + SOC2 artifacts exchange.
- Week 1-2: Perf POC on Dedicated mirror (32 GPUs reserved) — run synthetic clinical chat load and measure p95/p99. SE to capture kernel/perf traces.
- Week 3: Failover test across AZs to validate multi-zone routing and RTO claims.
- Week 4: Security review completion and KMS integration sign-off.

Key quotes & call snippets: 
- "We cannot accept anything less than near five-nines for clinician workflows — patient safety depends on it." — Head of Platform (Orchid Harbor).
- "If you can give a deterministic credit schedule tied to uptime bands and a clear maintenance policy, procurement is ready to move." — Procurement lead.

Open action items: 
- Redwood legal: draft SLA annex with 99.995% uplift option + proposed credit schedule (Jordan).
- SE (Maya): produce perf report from Dedicated demo with p50/p95/p99 numbers and kernel selection notes; include suggested batching / kv-cache config.
- Security: supply ISO/SOC evidence and KMS integration runbook (link in drive).
- Commercial: price premium for 99.995% and dedicated SRE on-call; include reserved GPU pricing schedule and burst policy.
